To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FGF12 binds to some, not all NaV CTs, and that a proline in the core domain contributes to the specificity of the FHF-NaV interaction.
FGF12 interacts with NaV1.1 and NaV1.4 CTs and that this interaction is required for proper subcellular localization of FGF12.
the interaction between FGF12 and NaV1.2 CTs is specific and requires the P149Q surface proline in FGF12.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of novel interaction sites that determine the specificity between fibroblast growth factor (FGF) homologous factors and voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) proteins, and the consequences of these interactions on the modulation of neuronal function.
the regulation of voltage-gated sodium (Na+) channels by fibroblast growth factor (FGF) homologous factor (FHFs, or FGF11–FGF14) proteins.
the regulation of ion channels and the mechanisms by which proteins regulate the gating properties of ion channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FGF12 binds with a higher affinity to the NaV1.x C termini than FGF12P149Q and that this differential binding affinity is a key determinant of specificity between FGF12 and the NaV1 CT.
the FGF12 P149Q polymorphism is a gain-of-function mutation that alters the interaction between FGF12 and NaV1.1, leading to increased Na+ channel activity.
the FGF12B binding site on the NaV 1.5 C-terminal tail is located between amino acids 1600 and 1625, and the interaction is mediated by two regions of the FGF12 B C-terminal tail.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel surface proline in the core domain that determines specificity between FGF12 and NaV1.2, and this proline contributes to a part of this specificity.

the FGF12 P149Q mutation, a human single nucleotic polymorphism, causes the FGF12 protein to lose its ability to bind to the NaV1.x channel C-terminal domain, resulting in the inability of FGF12 P148 to target to the axon-initial segment and modulate the NaV1 current.
the specificity in the interaction between FGF12 and NaV1 CT is mediated by both surface residues and affinity of the binding partner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple determinants that mediate specificity between FHFs and voltage-gated sodium channel C termini, and that these determinants are not necessarily conserved across the family.
the specificity of FHF-VGSC interaction is not only dependent upon the amino acid sequence but also on the affinity of the interaction.

the FHF family of proteins has a high level of specificity in their interaction with voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) isoforms, and that this specificity is determined by both protein-protein interactions and protein-protein affinity.
